question: What is the primary goal of using aseptic techniques during immunization?

options.A: To prevent the introduction of harmful pathogens into the body
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the client
options.C: To speed up the total vaccination process
options.D: To ensure the vaccine liquid remains ice cold

explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed to stop germs from contaminating sterile equipment and entering the client's body during a procedure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: Why is a skin puncture considered a critical moment for infection control?

options.A: It forces the nurse to use personal protective equipment
options.B: It increases the chemical potency of the vaccine
options.C: It immediately causes allergic reactions in patients
options.D: It breaks the body's natural primary defense barrier

explanation: The skin is our first line of defense against microorganisms; piercing it creates a direct pathway into deep tissues and the bloodstream if germs are present. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: When should a nurse use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When the clinic runs out of clean disposable gloves
options.B: Only at the very beginning of the morning shift
options.C: Before opening every single new vaccine vial
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Soap and water are required to physically wash away visible dirt, grime, and certain types of spores that alcohol rubs cannot clear effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: What makes friction the most important part of the handwashing process?

options.A: It warms up the water to kill resistant bacterial spores
options.B: It creates bubbles that dry out the skin's outer layer
options.C: It physically removes transient microorganisms from skin surfaces
options.D: It activates the antiseptic chemicals inside standard soap

explanation: The rubbing action of friction is what actually loosens and sweeps away transient germs clinging to the oils on your hands. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: Why must you wait for the alcohol swab on a vial stopper to air dry?

options.A: Drying is required for the alcohol to kill microorganisms effectively
options.B: It prevents the needle from slipping out of your fingers
options.C: Chemicals in wet alcohol deactivate the live vaccine virus
options.D: Wet alcohol ruins the rubber stopper and causes leaks

explanation: Alcohol needs a short amount of evaporation time to disrupt cell membranes and destroy bacteria on the rubber surface. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a needle stuck in a multidose vaccine vial?

options.A: It changes the recommended dosage for pediatric clients
options.B: It provides an easy entry route for environmental bacteria
options.C: It causes the liquid vaccine to freeze too quickly
options.D: It increases the expiration date printed on the label

explanation: Leaving a needle in the stopper breaks the closed seal of the vial, allowing airborne or contact germs to contaminate the remaining doses inside. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: In what pattern should you clean an injection site with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Up and down in long vertical strokes only
options.B: In a circular motion from the center moving outward
options.C: From the outer edges inward toward the exact center
options.D: In a harsh side-to-side scrubbing motion across the skin

explanation: Cleaning from the center outward pushes dirt and bacteria away from the spot where the needle will enter the skin. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: A nurse cleans a child's thigh for a vaccine, but then touches the exact spot with a bare finger to check the muscle landmark. What is the correct action?

options.A: Proceed with the injection since the finger was recently washed
options.B: Wipe the skin with a dry cotton ball and give the vaccine
options.C: Change the needle on the syringe and inject immediately
options.D: Clean the skin again with a new alcohol swab and let it dry

explanation: Touching the cleansed skin with a bare finger contaminates the site, requiring the nurse to repeat the skin cleaning step before proceeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: What is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries after giving an injection?

options.B: Always recap needles using two hands
options.C: Bend the needle before throwing it away
options.D: Store used needles in your uniform pocket

explanation: Trying to put a cap back onto a used needle is the leading cause of accidental puncture wounds in healthcare practice. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: When should a sharps disposal container be safely sealed and replaced?

options.A: Only when it is completely overflowing at the top
options.B: At the very end of every calendar month
options.C: When it reaches the three-quarters full mark
options.D: As soon as the first single syringe is dropped inside

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters full prevents needles from poking out of the opening and endangering staff who handle the waste. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: Which item belongs inside the yellow infectious waste bin during an immunization session?

options.A: Food wrappers left over from the outreach lunch break
options.B: Cardboard packaging boxes that held the vaccine vials
options.C: Cotton swabs stained with blood or vaccine fluid
options.D: Empty plastic water bottles brought by clinic staff

explanation: Items contaminated with body fluids or biological residues must go into biohazard infectious bins to prevent contamination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: Why is correct waste segregation at the primary healthcare level so critical?

options.A: It makes the clinic storeroom look neat for visiting supervisors
options.B: It ensures that general waste burns at a much lower temperature
options.C: It protects community waste handlers from accidental injuries and infections
options.D: It allows the clinic to recycle all used plastic syringes into new toys

explanation: Proper sorting ensures that hazardous items like needles and blood-soaked cotton do not end up in municipal dumps where they can harm the public. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)
